title: His best pupils: Adolph Alexander and George
summary: Picou names Adolph Alexander and an older pupil George, still playing on Royal Street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: How long have you spent sometimes with one pupil? I mean, have you worked with one boy over many years? Or is it just a matter of months? How long does it usually take for you to teach somebody? Well... What's the longest you ever took?
The best one I had, it was a year, a night before that. They call him Alexander. Alexander?
Adolph Alexander. Adolph Alexander. Adolph Alexander, that's what I'm...

Who do you think was the best of your own pupils on clarinet? I don't remember that. If you had to pick out the best of the musicians that you taught, who would you think was the best of them? I can't get you there.

George, George, George. We had our picture taken some time ago. Is he still paying? Oh yeah. Uh huh. Here in New Orleans? Yeah. He's with... He's with... He's with... I follow the Royal Street there. . .
Is he a young fellow? No. Oh, I see.

Does he play every night, you mean? He plays every night now? No. I wonder if he was on Royal Street, if he played someplace on Royal Street? Yes, he do. But I believe it's three of... About three times a week. Three times a week. Yes.
